This exercise examines where recorded armed conflict clusters across Myanmar's **330 townships**, and how those patterns evolve over **57 months**, from January 2021 to September 2025.

## Submission links

- **[Technical report](technical-report.qmd)** — data audit, complete R workflow, township counts, Local Moran's I, Gi*, emerging hotspot analysis and a conditional spatial scan.
- **[Executive summary](executive-summary.qmd)** — a Quarto revealjs presentation with nine substantive slides, plus a cover and contents slide.
- **[GitHub project](https://github.com/zhenhuaArhci/isss626-coursework/tree/main/take-home%20exercise2)** — Quarto sources, modular R scripts, aggregated results and reproduction instructions.

## Research questions

1. Which townships form statistically significant concentrations or spatial outliers in recorded armed events and violence against civilians?
2. Where is the relative concentration of conflict intensifying, diminishing or changing intermittently?
3. Which spatial clusters gained a larger share of events in January–September 2025 compared with the same months of 2024?

![](figures/01-township-counts.png){fig-alt="Two township choropleth maps showing total armed events and violence-against-civilians events."}

## Data and interpretation

The analysis uses the supplied **ACLED Myanmar January 2021–September 2025** extract and the specified **MIMU township boundaries v9.4**. Raw records, vector boundaries and event-level intermediates remain local. The website publishes analytical figures and township aggregates.

A hotspot is a relative concentration of **recorded events**. A cold spot does not establish safety, and a zero is no recorded included event in that cell. These historical results support contextual humanitarian assessment; they do not establish current access conditions or predict individual incidents.
